description: Buen día soy Adrián Ruiz líder del equipo Root Crew Code tengo amplia experiencia en el área de software y ingeniería lo que busco en mi equipo es compromiso, ganas de aprender, trabajo en equipo, conocimiento técnico, sobre todo lógica de programación qué entiendan lo que están haciendo
summary: VeraScope is a web app that answers a simple question about any place on Earth: is this a real long-term change in the climate, or just El Niño? For each 0.5° cell, it analyzes monthly NASA POWER (MERRA-2) data from 1981 to 2025 twice: on the original series and on the series with the El Niño signal removed. Comparing both trends gives one of four verdicts: robust change, sensitive to El Niño, hidden change, or no detectable trend. It also scans 4,235 cells across 5 variables with false-discovery control and draws lines across the Pacific between regions that move together during El Niño, such as Piura (Peru) and the western Pacific. This matters because extreme ENSO years are often mistaken for trends. VeraScope separates the two honestly and treats "no detectable trend" as a valid finding.
details:
What it does: In the browser, the user picks a variable (rainfall, temperature, root-zone and surface soil moisture, or relative humidity) and clicks a place on a Pacific-centered map. The app shows a verdict card and three synced charts: Cause (El Niño index), Consequence (standardized anomalies of the cell and its remote partner), and Reality (the original or El Niño-free series with its trend line). A "Remove El Niño" switch updates the charts and the verdict instantly, with no extra network calls. A time player animates the data month by month and lights up the teleconnection lines in the months when both regions are affected together.

How it works: A FastAPI backend pulls monthly series from NASA POWER and builds monthly anomalies. It removes the El Niño signal by joint regression with the trend (0-6 month lags, using NOAA CPC's Oceanic Niño Index, with Niño 1+2 as a complementary index for coastal Peru). It estimates trends with Theil-Sen and an autocorrelation-corrected Mann-Kendall test (Hamed-Rao), with confidence intervals consistent with the p-value. ScanMap applies Benjamini-Hochberg to all tests, and correlations use the effective sample size. The web app never computes statistics; it only displays what the API returns, always with source, unit, cell, and period.

Tools: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, and pandas for the backend (hosted on Render); React Native for Web with Expo, TypeScript, react-native-svg, and D3 for our own map and charts (hosted on Netlify); Jest and pytest for testing.

Impact and honesty: VeraScope helps farmers, planners, and students in places like northern Peru tell real change apart from ENSO variability. We never claim causation: linked regions "occur at the same time and both respond to El Niño."
